subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which prominent founding leader of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh propounded the philosophy of 'Integral Humanism'?
questions.explanation: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya formulated the philosophy of 'Integral Humanism' in 1965, presenting an indigenous socio-economic model distinct from Western capitalism and Marxism.

questions.question: In which year did the Communist Party of India (CPI) split into two distinct political parties: the CPI and the CPI(Marxist)?
questions.explanation: The CPI formally split in 1964 into the pro-Soviet CPI and the pro-Beijing/independent CPI(M) amidst the Sino-Soviet ideological rift and the 1962 border war.

questions.question: The Dewan of which southern princely state created a national sensation in 1947 by announcing the state's determination to declare complete independence?
questions.explanation: Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar, the Dewan of Travancore, initially declared that Travancore would remain an independent sovereign state, before popular pressure forced accession.

questions.question: The state of Haryana was carved out of Punjab on linguistic grounds in which year following the Shah Commission recommendations?
questions.explanation: Punjab was reorganised on 1 November 1966 into Punjabi-speaking Punjab and Hindi-speaking Haryana, with Chandigarh designated as a shared Union Territory.

questions.question: Which autonomous statutory body was established in 1965 to recommend remunerative Minimum Support Prices (MSP) to safeguard farmers' incomes?
options: B) National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED)
D) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explanation: The Agricultural Prices Commission (later renamed the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices, CACP) was set up in January 1965 to advise on agricultural price policy and MSP.

questions.question: Which of the following was a primary negative socio-economic consequence of the Green Revolution in rural India?
options: A) It completely wiped out wheat and rice cultivation across northwestern India
B) It intensified regional disparities and widened the economic gap between prosperous landlords and landless agricultural laborers
C) It compelled all Indian farmers to abandon cooperative credit institutions
D) It caused a collapse in the national foodgrain buffer stocks maintained by the FCI
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution concentrated benefits in affluent regions (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) and enriched big landowners, leaving dryland regions and small tenant farmers marginalized.

questions.question: In which month and year did India conduct a series of five underground nuclear weapon tests under 'Operation Shakti' at Pokhran?
questions.explanation: Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, India conducted five underground nuclear tests at Pokhran on 11 and 13 May 1998, establishing itself as a nuclear weapons state.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which veteran Congress leader served as the Congress President in 1969 who formally issued the order expelling Prime Minister Indira Gandhi from the party?
questions.explanation: Congress President S. Nijalingappa, representing the Syndicate, expelled Indira Gandhi from the primary membership of the party on 12 November 1969 for indiscipline.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act passed during the Emergency extended the duration of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from five to six years?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies to six years, which was later restored to five years by the 44th Amendment.

questions.question: Which political party formed the state government in Assam in December 1985 following the signing of the historic Assam Accord?
questions.explanation: Student leaders of AASU formed the regional party Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) in October 1985, swept the state assembly elections, and Prafulla Kumar Mahanta became Chief Minister.

questions.question: The Self-Respect Movement (Suyamariyathai Iyakkam) in Tamil Nadu, which laid the ideological foundation for Dravidian politics, was pioneered by:
questions.explanation: Periyar E.V. Ramasamy launched the Self-Respect Movement in 1925, advocating rationalism, anti-caste egalitarianism, and Dravidian cultural revival.

questions.question: On which auspicious occasion was the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) formally launched by grassroots activist Kanshi Ram?
options: D) 14 April 1984 (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's birth anniversary)
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram formally established the Bahujan Samaj Party on 14 April 1984, on the birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, to capture political power for Bahujan society.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which Soviet leader famously introduced 'Glasnost' (Openness) allowing freedom of speech and public criticism of the Communist regime?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev initiated Glasnost (policy of openness) in the late 1980s, dismantling state censorship of the media and encouraging open intellectual discourse.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following countries was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012 for over six decades of advancing peace, reconciliation, and human rights?
questions.explanation: The European Union was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012 in recognition of its role in transforming Europe from a continent of war into a continent of enduring peace.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which Indian Prime Minister initiated the landmark 'Look East' policy in 1991 to forge economic ties with Southeast Asian nations?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao launched India's 'Look East' policy in 1991, orienting India's strategic and trade engagements towards ASEAN and East Asia.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Who was the founder-leader of the Awami League who led the Bangladesh liberation movement and became the first Prime Minister of Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman spearheaded the autonomy movement in East Pakistan, proclaimed Bangladesh's independence, and served as its founding head of state.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: The Sinhala Only Act (Official Language Act No. 33), which sparked deep ethnic alienation among Tamils in Sri Lanka, was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Sri Lankan Parliament enacted the Sinhala Only Act in 1956 under Prime Minister S.W.R.D. Bandaranaike, recognizing Sinhala as the sole official language.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Where is the permanent headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) located?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (the principal judicial organ of the UN) is seated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which international treaty adopted in Paris in December 2015 aims to limit the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement on Climate Change was adopted at COP21 in December 2015, replacing the Kyoto Protocol with nationally determined emission targets.

questions.question: Which set of free-market policy prescriptions advocated by the IMF and World Bank emphasizing deregulation, privatisation, and trade liberalisation is termed the:
questions.explanation: The 'Washington Consensus' refers to a package of neo-liberal economic reform policies promoted by Washington-based institutions for developing crisis-hit nations.

questions.question: What theory did socialist leader Asoka Mehta propound to justify constructive cooperation with the Nehru government during the 1950s?
options: A) The political compulsions of an underdeveloped economy
B) The inevitable dictatorship of the proletariat
C) The total negation of bourgeois parliamentary institutions
D) The unconditional merger of socialist cadre with the Swatantra Party
questions.explanation: Asoka Mehta argued that an underdeveloped nation like India faced developmental compulsions requiring cooperation between progressive democratic forces and the ruling party.

questions.question: Under which constitutional draft and administrative compromise was Article 370 originally incorporated into the Indian Constitution?
options: A) As a permanent, unalterable basic structure article drafted personally by Sardar Patel
B) As a 'temporary, transitional and special provision' negotiated by Gopalaswami Ayyangar and Sheikh Abdullah
C) As a conditional bilateral pact overseen by the United Nations Military Observer Group
D) As an emergency decree promulgated under the Government of India Act 1935
questions.explanation: Article 370 was framed by N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar as a temporary provision in Part XXI of the Constitution, reflecting the unique transitional circumstances of Kashmir's accession.

questions.question: Which historic parliamentary statute enacted in 1971 reorganized the entire northeastern region of India, conferring statehood on Meghalaya, Manipur, and Tripura?
questions.explanation: The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 elevated the Union Territories of Manipur and Tripura and the autonomous sub-state of Meghalaya to full statehood.

questions.question: In which three industrial locations were major public sector iron and steel manufacturing plants established with foreign collaboration during the Second Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: During the Second Plan (1956-61), steel plants were erected with foreign partnership at Bhilai (Soviet assistance), Rourkela (West German assistance), and Durgapur (British assistance).

questions.question: What is the core strategic commitment governing India's official nuclear doctrine adopted in January 2003?
options: A) 'No First Use' (NFU) and credible minimum nuclear deterrence with massive retaliation in response to any nuclear attack
B) Preemptive launch on warning against any hostile neighbor accumulating ballistic missiles
C) Complete renunciation of nuclear warheads and unilateral accession to the NPT without conditions
D) Automatic nuclear retaliation triggered whenever conventional border artillery skirmishes occur
questions.explanation: India's nuclear doctrine commits to 'No First Use', meaning nuclear weapons will only be used in retaliation against a nuclear strike, alongside credible minimum deterrence.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In which landmark 1967 verdict did the Supreme Court of India rule by a 6:5 majority that Parliament had no power to abridge Fundamental Rights through constitutional amendments?
options: A) Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
B) Golaknath v. State of Punjab
C) Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
D) Minerva Mills v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In Golaknath (1967), Chief Justice K. Subba Rao ruled that Fundamental Rights enjoy a transcendental position and Parliament cannot curtail them even under Article 368.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which controversial constitutional amendment passed in August 1975 sought to place the election of the Prime Minister and Lok Sabha Speaker beyond judicial review?
questions.explanation: The 39th Amendment was enacted specifically to nullify the Allahabad High Court verdict against Indira Gandhi by placing the election of the President, VP, PM, and Speaker beyond court scrutiny.

questions.question: In the general elections of March 1977, in which constituencies were Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay Gandhi defeated by opposition candidates?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi lost Rae Bareli to Raj Narain by over 55,000 votes, and Sanjay Gandhi lost neighboring Amethi to Ravindra Pratap Singh of the Janata Party.

questions.question: Why did the first non-Congress Janata Party government collapse prematurely in July 1979 after barely 28 months in power?
options: A) Due to fierce internal factional disputes and the controversy over the 'dual membership' of former Jana Sangh members in the RSS
B) Due to the nationwide military coup staged by the armed forces commanders
C) Due to an absolute majority floor revolt led by the Communist Party of India
D) Due to a declaration of financial emergency under Article 360 by the President
questions.explanation: Factional rivalries between Morarji Desai, Charan Singh, and Jagjivan Ram, combined with the dispute over former Jana Sangh leaders' simultaneous RSS membership, fractured the Janata Party.

questions.question: Which militant Sikh preacher emerged as the prominent leader advocating armed militancy and occupied the Akal Takht prior to Operation Blue Star in 1984?
questions.explanation: Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale transformed Sikh politics into an armed confrontation, stockpiling weapons inside the Golden Temple complex until his death in Operation Blue Star.

questions.question: What triggered the withdrawal of support by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from V.P. Singh's National Front government in October 1990?
options: A) The signing of the World Trade Organization accession charter in Geneva
B) The nationwide implementation of the New Economic Policy by the Union Cabinet
C) The arrest of BJP President L.K. Advani in Samastipur, Bihar, during his Ayodhya Ram Rath Yatra
D) The deployment of the Indian Army in Jammu and Kashmir under AFSPA
questions.explanation: When Lalu Prasad Yadav's government arrested L.K. Advani at Samastipur during the Rath Yatra to Ayodhya, the BJP withdrew its external support, causing V.P. Singh's government to fall.

questions.question: Which commission of inquiry was constituted by the Government of India in December 1992 to investigate the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya?
questions.explanation: The Liberhan Ayodhya Commission of Inquiry was established under retired High Court Judge M.S. Liberhan to probe the sequence of events leading to the demolition of the Babri structure.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What was the popular name given to the massive privatization vouchers distributed to Russian citizens during Shock Therapy that were swiftly snapped up by the mafia and black marketers?
questions.explanation: Russian citizens were issued vouchers with a nominal value of 10,000 rubles to buy shares in state enterprises, but desperation led millions to sell them for petty cash.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: The Treaty of Rome signed in March 1957 by six Western European countries created which two seminal supranational organisations?
options: A) European Union (EU) and European Central Bank (ECB)
B) European Economic Community (EEC) and European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom)
C) Council of Europe and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO)
D) Western European Union and European Monetary Fund
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Rome was signed by France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg, creating the EEC (Common Market) and Euratom.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What economic phenomenon enabled South Korea to rapidly transform from an impoverished war-torn society into a high-income industrial giant between the 1960s and 1990s?
options: C) The Miracle on the Han River
questions.explanation: South Korea's export-led rapid economic growth, driven by giant industrial conglomerates (Chaebols) and heavy state investment, is known as the 'Miracle on the Han River'.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In Nepal, which multi-party political coalition spearheaded the massive 2006 popular movement (Jana Andolan II) against the direct autocratic rule of King Gyanendra?
questions.explanation: The Seven Party Alliance (SPA), comprising all major democratic parties, joined hands with the underground Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) to lead the April 2006 mass democracy movement.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which principal organ of the United Nations officially suspended its operations in 1994 following the independence of Palau, the last remaining UN trust territory?
options: B) The Economic and Social Council
C) The International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: The UN Trusteeship Council suspended active operations on 1 November 1994 after Palau, the final trust territory administered by the United States, attained independence.

questions.question: Which bilateral disarmament treaty signed between the US and the USSR in 1972 severely restricted both superpowers from deploying missile interceptor defense systems?
questions.explanation: The ABM Treaty barred the deployment of nationwide missile defense systems to preserve the logic of mutual assured destruction (MAD); the US unilaterally withdrew in 2002.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which United Nations body based in Nairobi, Kenya, was set up following the 1972 Stockholm Conference to coordinate international environmental activities?
options: D) Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
questions.explanation: UNEP was established in 1972 headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, serving as the leading global environmental authority within the UN system.

questions.question: How does the phenomenon of 'Cultural Heterogenisation' challenge the pessimistic thesis that globalisation merely imposes Western cultural uniformity?
options: A) By proving that all modern non-Western nations have completely banned Western television and consumer products
B) By asserting that ancient indigenous folklore will automatically replace Western scientific technology globally
C) By demonstrating that international trade agreements enforce strict religious orthodoxy across all nations
D) By showing that external cultural influences are modified and blended with local traditions, generating new unique hybrid cultural forms ('glocalisation')
questions.explanation: Cultural heterogenisation argues that globalisation does not lead to simple Americanisation, but creates vibrant hybrid combinations (such as Khadi jeans or paneer pizza) where each culture retains distinct flavor.

questions.question: Which political faction was recognized as the official Opposition in the Fourth Lok Sabha (1969) for the first time in Indian parliamentary history, with Ram Subhag Singh as Leader of Opposition?
questions.explanation: Following the 1969 split, Congress(O) secured over 60 Lok Sabha seats, qualifying for the 10% threshold to obtain the official status of Opposition party under Dr. Ram Subhag Singh.

questions.question: In which princely state was a violent peasant uprising against forced grain levies (vetti) and feudal landlords spearheaded by the Communists between 1946 and 1951?
options: B) Telangana region of Hyderabad state
questions.explanation: The Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle was waged against the feudal Deshmukhs and Razakars under the Nizam of Hyderabad from 1946 until it was called off by the CPI in 1951.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment abolished the constitutional recognition and guarantee of private property as a Fundamental Right, transferring it to an ordinary legal right under Article 300A?
questions.explanation: The Janata Party government through the 44th Amendment in 1978 omitted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, demoting the Right to Property to a non-fundamental legal right under Article 300A.

questions.question: Which high-altitude territory across the Ladakh border was clandestinely traversed and paved by China in the late 1950s to build a strategic highway linking Tibet with Xinjiang?
questions.explanation: China constructed National Highway 219 across the uninhabited Aksai Chin plateau of Ladakh between 1956 and 1957, discovery of which triggered intense Indo-China border clashes.

questions.question: Which senior jurist and civil liberties advocate represented petitioner Raj Narain before Justice J.L. Sinha in the famous 1975 election petition against Indira Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Shanti Bhushan argued the case on behalf of socialist leader Raj Narain, successfully proving that Indira Gandhi's election agent Yashpal Kapur worked on the campaign before his resignation was gazetted.

questions.question: Under the 1985 Punjab Accord, which specific judicial tribunal was designated to adjudicate the contentious sharing of the Ravi-Beas river waters between Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Punjab Accord mandated the appointment of a Supreme Court judge to head the Ravi-Beas Waters Tribunal; Justice V. Balakrishna Eradi was appointed in April 1986.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which enclave in the South Caucasus was the focus of a bitter inter-ethnic military conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan as the Soviet Union disintegrated?
questions.explanation: Nagorno-Karabakh, an Armenian-majority autonomous oblast inside the Azerbaijan SSR, declared independence in 1988, sparking a brutal war between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which international agreement signed in 1995 officially established the institutional framework of the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) utilizing the Common Effective Preferential Tariff (CEPT) scheme?
options: A) The Manila Protocol on Counter-Terrorism
B) The Jakarta Declaration on Currency Pegging
C) The Bali Accord on Military Non-Intervention
D) The Singapore Summit Declaration (1992) and Chiang Mai protocol
questions.explanation: AFTA was enacted through the CEPT scheme agreed at the Singapore Summit in 1992 and expanded in the 1995 Bangkok Summit to progressively reduce tariffs among member nations.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: In the governance structure of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), what determines each member country's voting power and financial commitment?
options: A) Quota subscription based on the country's relative weight in the global economy
B) An equal one-member one-vote distribution identical to the UN General Assembly
C) The size of the member country's standing armed forces registered with the UN
D) The geographical land area of the member country certified by UNESCO
questions.explanation: Voting rights in the IMF are determined by quotas calculated on GDP, openness, economic variability, and international reserves, giving the US and EU decisive veto thresholds.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which non-governmental international coalition was established in 1975 to represent indigenous communities across continents and gained consultative status with the UN ECOSOC in 1977?
options: C) World Council of Indigenous Peoples (WCIP)
questions.explanation: The World Council of Indigenous Peoples (WCIP) was formed in 1975 in Port Alberni, Canada, bringing indigenous voices to the UN and pioneering the draft declaration on indigenous rights.
